title: Change the caller's list, not the caller's variable

blocks.text: Java passes every argument by value. For an object, the value is a copy of the reference: the method and the caller point to the same object, so a change to the object is seen by the caller, while assigning a new object to the parameter only changes the method's copy.
Write `addAll(List<String> target, String... items)` in `Collector`. It adds every non-null item to the caller's own `target` list, in order, and returns how many it added:

cases.says: addAll returns how many items it added.
The caller's own list holds the new items afterwards.
null items are skipped, and not counted.

concepts: A method receives a copy of a reference: changes to the object it points to reach the caller, reassigning the parameter does not.
